messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@legacybank.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@legacybank.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment follow-up & hardware questions

Hi Alice / Tom —

Great to meet with you today. Per our call, here’s a short recap and next steps so we’re all aligned on the on-prem air-gapped qualification work for LegacyBank: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary requirement: fully air-gapped deployment inside LegacyBank data centers (no outbound internet egress).
- Data residency & compliance: HSM/KMS integration required; SOC2 + audit log exports for customer-facing controls.
- Scale profile: ~300 RPS peak for text generation, average 60k tokens/minute, burst capacity for month-end jobs.
- Availability: N+1 within a single site initially, with potential cross-site replication later.
- Ops constraints: change windows limited to weekends; limited connectivity for remote support (we’ll need an approved jump host process).

Questions we raised (from Redwood)
1) Rack space / power: Do you have existing rack U availability and PDU capacity per rack?
2) Upgrade path: How do you prefer hardware upgrades — scheduled on-site windows, or do you want a lift-and-shift style replacement?
3) Offline ops: Who on your ops team owns firmware/BIOS updates for air-gapped hardware?
4) KMS/HSM: Which vendor/version (Thales/Vormetric/HashiCorp + HSM model) do you use for key wrapping?

Attachments we’ll send: hardware spec sheet, airgap install guide, network diagram.

Next steps
- I’ll share the hardware spec and our recommended rack layout (Dev is looping to provide details).
- Dev will propose an offline upgrade & maintenance workflow we’ve used on previous air-gapped installs.
- Schedule a 45-min SE deep-dive next week to validate network/firewall and KMS requirements.

Please confirm the best times for a follow-up (we’re tentatively holding Wed/Thu mornings PT). Also, Tom — if you can share the rack PDU details and the ops contact for firmware, that will help us prepare a tighter checklist.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this to the qualification phase.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Rack space / power: We have 2 racks available in DC-13 with dual PDUs (30A per PDU). Rack U is limited to 42U but one rack is already half populated. I can share exact U allocations.
- Firmware/BIOS: Our infra team (Sanjay) manages firmware updates; they require 2-week ETA and a maintenance window.
- KMS/HSM: We’re on Thales HSM (Luna SA 7) and use a key wrapping approach — orientation is that keys remain in HSM, Redwood will use wrapped keys via our offline key exchange process.

I’ve attached the rack elevations and PDU spec (see attachment stub). Can Dev share an estimated rack layout and power draw so we can validate?

Tom
Tom Ellis
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, LegacyBank

Hi Tom / Alice —

Thanks for the detail, Tom — that helps a lot. I’ve attached our recommended rack layout and a hardware spec sheet that shows power draw, cooling requirements, and recommended GPU counts per node. Short notes below: 

- Reference config: 4x 4U servers (dual-socket, 8x A100-80GB style GPUs per server) per rack gives us the capacity for your target throughput with N+1 redundancy. Total rack power draw estimated at ~10.5kW under peak.
- PDU suggestion: dual PDUs with breakers sized for 30A per leg — aligns with what you described. We can spread servers across both PDUs.
- Offline upgrade approach: We do staged upgrade windows — spin a maintenance VM on a test node, snapshot KV caches, swap hardware, validate under synthetic traffic, then bring back into live set. For air-gapped installs, we provide an on-prem install playbook (attached) and a signed checklist for each maintenance window.
- KMS integration: We support wrapped keys via a manual key import process and can work with Thales Luna for a signed key exchange. Michael — can you confirm any additional audit/logging requirements for the SOC2 evidence?

Proposed next steps:
1) Shared drive: I uploaded the full spec + rack diagram to the folder linked below.
2) SE deep-dive: Wed 13 May, 09:00 PT (12:00 ET) — 45 minutes to review firewall rules, jump host process, and KMS exchange checklist.
3) Ops contact: Tom to introduce Sanjay (ops) to Michael for audit/logging questions.

Links / attachments: onprem-hardware-specs.pdf, airgap-install-guide.pdf, network-diagram.png 

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
